title: Brief — cap the browse-band card max

set.request: One small fix from the site study's stage verdict: cap the per-card max in ext/catalog/browse.css's `.browse-band > .page-previews` from a bare `1fr` to `min(28em, 1fr)`, the same shape wall() already uses, so a short band (2-3 cards) stops stretching cards to ~1000px at 3440. Verify headless at 1280 and 3440 on three pages with short bands, one before/after shot pair at 3440, doc a line in ext/catalog/readme.md Watch out and doc/decisions.md.
set.now: documentation: readme.md Watch out line + dated doc/decisions.md line
steps: read browse.css, wall()'s Page.css rule, and the site-study verdict + decision line
find every real caller of Page.prototype.browse() to identify pages with short (2-3 card) bands
start the private server on PORT=8132
measure widest card in a short band before the fix, at 1280 and 3440, on three candidate pages
make the one CSS change in browse.css's theme layer
re-measure the same three pages after the fix at 1280 and 3440, confirm no band narrower than before at 1280 and zero console errors
shoot one before/after pair at 3440, kill the private server by its real PID
documentation: readme.md Watch out line + dated doc/decisions.md line
set.outcome:
**A short `browse()` band no longer stretches its cards past 28em.** One line in `ext/catalog/browse.css`: `.browse-band > .page-previews > .page-preview { max-width: 28em }` — about 421px at 1280, 504px at 3440 (the site's fluid body font-size, `framework.css`'s clamp). Verified on the real bug, not a guess: `/framework/core/Layout/`'s Tags facet filtered to `landing` leaves exactly 2 cards in one band — measured 1347px each at 3440 before the fix, 504px after. Two more pages (`/framework/ui/`, `/framework/core/Page/`) confirmed unaffected — their widest bands were already under the cap. Every 1280 measurement on all three pages is byte-identical before and after (no band got narrower). Zero console errors in any phase.

The obvious version of this fix — mirroring `wall()`'s own `min(length, %)` shape onto the track's maximum, `minmax(MIN, min(28em, 1fr))` — is invalid CSS (`fr` cannot nest inside a generic `min()`) and broke the grid completely when tried live (every card jumped to 100% width, worse than the bug). Capping the card's own `max-width` instead leaves the grid's `auto-fit` track-count math untouched, which is what keeps 1280 provably unaffected. Full weighing table: [doc/decisions.md](/framework/ext/catalog/doc/decisions.md).
